title: Button input model - presses, holds, and chords
description:
Chris flagged: the engine needs a logical button model layered above raw PicoSystem button reads, not ad-hoc polling in the turn loop.

PicoSystem controls: A, B, X, Y face buttons + d-pad (Up/Down/Left/Right).

The model must support:
- Single press - edge-triggered, one action per press.
- Press-and-hold - (maybe) auto-repeat for movement, and/or a distinct long-press action. Decide.
- Button PAIRS / chords - definitely needed: e.g. Up+X, A+B, and other pairs, as distinct actions. Decide press-vs-hold semantics for chords, the simultaneity window for 'pressed together', and how firing a chord suppresses the two individual-button actions.

One chord is reserved to enter diagnostic mode (see the diagnostic-mode bead).

Deliver an input module in Chapter_7/game/ that emits a documented event set consumed by the turn loop and menu/UI code, plus a doc of the full button map.
design:
Open questions to settle:
- Repeat rate + initial delay for held d-pad (movement); does hold ever mean something other than repeat?
- Chord detection: fixed time window vs 'both down on same poll'; debounce interval.
- Chord vs sequence: are we only doing simultaneous pairs, or also 2-button combos where order matters? (Start simple: simultaneous pairs only.)
- Event delivery: queue vs immediate callback; does the turn loop pull one event per turn?
- Which chords are bound (movement diagonals via Up+Right etc.? or d-pad diagonals handled separately)?
- List the reserved chords: diagnostic-mode toggle + any others (quick-inventory, quit-to-menu?).
acceptance_criteria: Input module in Chapter_7/game/ with a documented event enum/set; simultaneous-pair chord detection with a defined window + debounce; individual-button actions correctly suppressed when their chord fires; button-map + chord table written to a doc; unit-testable off-device (feed synthetic button states).

title: Turn model
description: Strict player->monsters vs energy/speed system; what one d-pad press does; diagonal movement?
design:
Strict round-robin scheduling, equal speed in v1: turn = resolve player action -> each monster acts once (fixed list order) -> upkeep. Actor turn-taking goes through a Scheduler seam (actors_for_turn()) so an integer-speed or full energy/action-point scheduler can replace it later as a STRETCH GOAL without touching AI/combat/turn-loop.

Movement: 4-way only (N/S/E/W), Manhattan distance, 4-neighbour adjacency - FOV/AI-pathing/combat-reach all built on this. 8-way is a deliberate revisit gate (like ART.md s9 perspective) - decide before cd-e3p.4/.5/.6 are final. One press = one tile step = one turn. Held direction = cd-e3p.11 auto-repeats single steps, rate-capped, pauses while a monster is in view. No auto-travel in v1.

Turn-consuming: move, attack, wait, item use, stairs. Free (no turn): failed move into wall, inventory/map view, diagnostic toggle, look mode. A wait action passes exactly one turn.

Presentation: instant tile snaps in v1; apply_move() (logical) split from the draw step (presentation) so tile-to-tile slide animation can be added later. Slides stay strict - player slide in player sub-turn, each monster slide in its sub-turn, sequential. Batching visible actors' slides into one concurrent tween is an open sub-decision for the animation bead.

Main loop: non-blocking fixed tick ~15-20fps; a turn advances only on an actionable input event; between turns only the anim pulse advances. cycle pulse = presentation heartbeat, NOT the turn counter (turn count is its own int).
notes: Written up in Chapter_7/doc/ENGINE.md s1. Downstream: cd-e3p.2 (fork), cd-e3p.3 (turn loop), cd-e3p.11 (input model - held-repeat + monster-in-view pause + reserved chords), and the future animation bead (batched-slide sub-decision) all build against s1.
close_reason: Turn model decided with Chris and recorded in Chapter_7/doc/ENGINE.md s1. Strict/equal-speed with a scheduler seam for later energy system; 4-way movement (revisit gate); snap-now/slide-later presentation split; non-blocking ~15-20fps loop.

title: On-device diagnostic mode - RAM/flash stats + short message log
description:
Chris flagged: once Ch7 runs on real PicoSystem hardware we will hit issues (OOM, load failures, slow turns) where on-device diagnostic data is the fastest path to a fix. Build a diagnostic mode now so it's ready.

Entry: a reserved button chord (defined in cd-e3p.11 button input model). Toggles a diagnostic overlay or dedicated screen.

Live stats to surface:
- Free / allocated RAM (gc.mem_free(), gc.mem_alloc()); peak / low-water if cheap to track.
- Flash / filesystem free (os.statvfs on CIRCUITPY).
- Frame time and per-turn time (ms); FPS.
- Current level seed, entity count, FOV/render cost.
- CircuitPython version + board id.

Diagnostic event log:
- Fixed-size ring buffer, SHORT entries to preserve RAM - store a compact code (e.g. 2-4 char code + optional small int arg), NOT full strings. Define a code table (e.g. LGEN start/done, LOAD fail, OOM near-miss, DESC level change).
- Rendered in the diagnostic screen, newest first.
- This is separate from the in-game player message log (cd-e3p.9) - different audience, tighter RAM budget.

Keep the whole thing small and guardable so it costs ~nothing when not shown.
design:
Decisions:
- Overlay on top of game vs full replacement screen (overlay is more useful mid-bug, costs more render).
- Ring buffer size (16? 32?) and entry struct (bytes vs small tuples).
- Code table location - shared module so engine code can log without importing UI.
- Is the log always recording (from boot) or only after diagnostic mode first opened? (Always recording is the point - catch the bug before you knew to look.)
- Any way to dump the log over serial/USB for off-device capture.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostic screen reachable via the reserved chord; shows RAM, flash, timing, seed, entity count, CP/board info; ring-buffer code log always recording from boot and displayed newest-first; documented code table; measured overhead when hidden is negligible (state it).
notes: Depends on cd-e3p.11 (chord to enter). Relates to cd-e3p.9 (player message log - keep the two distinct), cd-89o.2 (on-device bring-up), cd-e17.10 (on-device art verification).

title: Off-device art preview / review gate
description: Enlarged on-screen review of candidate sheets before anything is loaded onto the PicoSystem. build_tiles.py --preview emits: (1) 8x contact-sheet PNGs per sheet into Chapter_7/doc/preview/ (committed, diffable history), with tile-index labels + master palette strip; (2) an HTML review artifact with a zoom toggle (2x/4x/8x/12x), image-rendering:pixelated, each sheet on both dark and light backgrounds. Scale rationale: 2x ~= actual PicoSystem physical size on a ~109ppi monitor, 8x is the working size for judging a single tile, 10-16x for pixel-level dithering inspection. This is the off-device counterpart to cd-e17.10 (on-device verification) and runs each candidate/review/refine round.
design: Preview code lives in build_tiles.py (cd-e17.4 owns the --preview emitter), desktop-only Pillow, not copied to CIRCUITPY. Contact sheets committed as PNG; HTML artifact regenerated per round.
notes: Emitter BUILT as part of cd-e17.4: build_tiles.py --preview writes doc/preview/{terrain,creatures,heroes,objects}.png (8x labelled contact sheets, committed) + doc/preview/tiles.html (zoom 2/4/8/12x, light/dark bg, image-rendering:pixelated, sheet PNG embedded once per sheet).
